## Acceptance Tolerance Specification — Aluminium Housing Bore vs Steel Shaft (H7/h6, 42 mm nominal)

### 1. Reference Standards and Material Data

| Parameter | Value | Source / Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Fit system | ISO 286 (limits and fits) | ISO 286-1 (system), ISO 286-2 (tolerance tables) |
| Nominal size | 42.000 mm | Given |
| Reference temperature | 20 °C | Standard reference temperature for ISO fits |
| Aluminium housing CTE | 23.1 × 10⁻⁶ /K | Provided |
| Steel shaft CTE | 11.7 × 10⁻⁶ /K | Plain carbon / low alloy steel class value (e.g., per common engineering references such as ASM or machinery handbooks; grade-specific value to be confirmed if a specific steel grade is later selected) |
| Operating temperature range | −20 °C to +60 °C | Given |

### 2. Tolerance Bands at 20 °C (ISO 286-2, nominal 42 mm)

**Hole (H7):**
- Lower deviation: 0 µm
- Upper deviation: +25 µm
- Bore at 20 °C: **42.000 mm to 42.025 mm**

**Shaft (h6):**
- Upper deviation: 0 µm
- Lower deviation: −16 µm
- Shaft at 20 °C: **41.984 mm to 42.000 mm**

### 3. Thermal Expansion/Contraction — Aluminium Housing Bore

Formula: \(D_T = D_{20} \times [1 + \alpha_{Al} \times (T - 20)]\), with \(\alpha_{Al} = 23.1 \times 10^{-6}\) /K.

**At −20 °C (ΔT = −40 K):**
- \(D_{min} = 42.000 \times (1 - 23.1\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.000 \times 0.999076 = 41.961192\) mm
- \(D_{max} = 42.025 \times (1 - 23.1\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.025 \times 0.999076 = 41.986169\) mm

**At +60 °C (ΔT = +40 K):**
- \(D_{min} = 42.000 \times (1 + 23.1\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.000 \times 1.000924 = 42.038808\) mm
- \(D_{max} = 42.025 \times (1 + 23.1\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.025 \times 1.000924 = 42.063831\) mm

### 4. Thermal Expansion/Contraction — Steel Shaft

Formula: \(D_T = D_{20} \times [1 + \alpha_{steel} \times (T - 20)]\), with \(\alpha_{steel} = 11.7 \times 10^{-6}\) /K.

**At −20 °C (ΔT = −40 K):**
- \(D_{min} = 41.984 \times (1 - 11.7\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 41.984 \times 0.999532 = 41.964351\) mm
- \(D_{max} = 42.000 \times (1 - 11.7\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.000 \times 0.999532 = 41.980344\) mm

**At +60 °C (ΔT = +40 K):**
- \(D_{min} = 41.984 \times (1 + 11.7\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 41.984 \times 1.000468 = 42.003649\) mm
- \(D_{max} = 42.000 \times (1 + 11.7\times10^{-6} \times 40) = 42.000 \times 1.000468 = 42.019656\) mm

### 5. Clearance Analysis

Clearance = bore diameter − shaft diameter.

**At −20 °C:**
- Min clearance = smallest bore − largest shaft = 41.961192 − 41.980344 = **−0.019152 mm** (interference)
- Max clearance = largest bore − smallest shaft = 41.986169 − 41.964351 = **+0.021818 mm**

**At +60 °C:**
- Min clearance = smallest bore − largest shaft = 42.038808 − 42.019656 = **+0.019152 mm**
- Max clearance = largest bore − smallest shaft = 42.063831 − 42.003649 = **+0.060182 mm**

### 6. Summary Tables

**Bore tolerance band at 20 °C (H7):**
| Condition | Dimension (mm) |
|---|---|
| Minimum | 42.000 |
| Maximum | 42.025 |

**Worst-case bore dimensions:**
| Temperature | Minimum (mm) | Maximum (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| −20 °C | 41.961 | 41.986 |
| +60 °C | 42.039 | 42.064 |

**Shaft dimensions at temperature extremes (h6):**
| Temperature | Minimum (mm) | Maximum (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| −20 °C | 41.964 | 41.980 |
| +60 °C | 42.004 | 42.020 |

**Clearance analysis:**
| Temperature | Min clearance (mm) | Max clearance (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| −20 °C | −0.019 (interference) | +0.022 |
| +60 °C | +0.019 | +0.060 |

### 7. Validation

- Tolerance values cross-checked against ISO 286-2 for 42 mm nominal: H7 = 0/+25 µm, h6 = 0/−16 µm. ✓
- Thermal calculations verified by the alternative method \(\Delta D = D_{20} \times \alpha \times \Delta T\) added to \(D_{20}\):
  - Aluminium at −20 °C: 42.000 − 0.038808 = 41.961192 mm ✓
  - Aluminium at +60 °C: 42.000 + 0.038808 = 42.038808 mm ✓
  - Steel at −20 °C: 42.000 − 0.019656 = 41.980344 mm ✓
  - Steel at +60 °C: 42.000 + 0.019656 = 42.019656 mm ✓
- Units consistent (mm, K). ✓
- Steel CTE is class-level (plain carbon/low alloy); if a specific steel grade is later selected, the CTE and all shaft-derived values must be recalculated.

### 8. Design Note

At −20 °C the minimum clearance is negative: **interference up to 0.019 mm** can occur. If a clearance fit is required at all temperatures, a design review is recommended (e.g., increase the nominal clearance, change the fit, or reduce the operating cold limit).
